answer: The pulse multiplier is published, charged in summit, and violet lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1288 identities would post 1747 proofs and burn roughly 59 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
